body.statement: For every input \((G^{+},H,A,a,Y)\) satisfying the model assumptions, the machine whose schedule contains only \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{sc}},\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}},\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}},\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\) terminates and returns exactly one sound certificate. On each transition the stated local polynomial obligation holds and \(\mu_H\) decreases lexicographically. It returns \((F_H,\mathcal D_H^{\mathrm{den}},\mathfrak D_H)\), with \(O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H\), if and only if \(T_{a,H}(\theta_1)=T_{a,H}(\theta_2)\) for all \(\theta_1,\theta_2\in\Theta_H\) satisfying \(O_H(\theta_1)=O_H(\theta_2)\); otherwise it returns a support-exact global-twin box. Thus \(F_H\) is partial on the ambient simplex but covers the complete compatible fixed-support image on an identified branch. This strictly completes Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser for the declared fixed-support class without adding a selector context.
body.proof_tex:
By \(\textnormal{thm:transition-soundness-termination}\), every admitted transition strictly decreases the lexicographic measure \(\mu_H\in\mathbb N^5\). The well-foundedness argument in that theorem rules out an infinite execution. Hence every maximal execution is finite.

The schedule \(\mathfrak P_H\) first chooses one of the four named relations in its fixed priority order and then chooses the lexicographically least eligible token under the canonical encoding. The residual verifier likewise chooses the first passing candidate in encoded order. Thus a state has at most one scheduled successor. If that successor is residual, the transition consumes the sole residual token, sets the terminal flag, emits one certificate, and halts. No later certificate can be emitted. If no transition is accepted, maximality instead leaves a nonterminal state with no verifier-accepted successor. These alternatives are exhaustive for a finite maximal execution.

Suppose a formula certificate is emitted. By \(\textnormal{thm:certificate-soundness}\),
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H,\qquad
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)
 \quad\text{for all }\theta\in\Theta_H.
\tag{22}
\]
If \(\theta_1,\theta_2\in\Theta_H\) satisfy
\(O_H(\theta_1)=O_H(\theta_2)\), then (22) gives
\[
 T_{a,H}(\theta_1)
 =F_H\{O_H(\theta_1)\}
 =F_H\{O_H(\theta_2)\}
 =T_{a,H}(\theta_2).
\tag{23}
\]
Thus the target is constant on every observation fiber.

Suppose instead that a global-twin box is emitted. Its rational endpoints satisfy \(\ell_j<u_j\), so the box is nonempty; for example its coordinatewise midpoint belongs to it. Certificate soundness gives, for any \(b\) in that box,
\[
 \theta_b^+,\theta_b^-\in\Theta_H,\qquad
 O_H(\theta_b^+)=O_H(\theta_b^-),\qquad
 T_{a,H}(\theta_b^+)\ne T_{a,H}(\theta_b^-).
\tag{24}
\]
Equation (24) is an explicit observation fiber on which the target is not constant, so identification fails. It also supplies exact support \(H\) and strict positivity through certificate soundness.

Nothing in the four transition definitions proves that one of the finite residual projection or contrast candidates passes at every irreducible state. Accordingly the preceding argument proves the stated formula implication, twin implication, uniqueness, and finite stuck-state alternative, but not the unsupported converse.
body.justification: This remains the field-level target: it would upgrade the proved normalization, scheduling, and certificate semantics to a complete fixed-support causal identification calculus.
body.gap: The exact unresolved gap is the all-residual rational-projection-or-common-contrast converse, including exclusion of an identified residual whose functional is algebraic but nonrational.
body.consumer: A complete dosearch backend with exhaustive model-level semantics must wait for this residual theorem; the proved positive and ordinary-ID layers can already be regression-tested.

obligation.what_is_open: The general residual converse: every irreducible fixed-support residual must contain either a verifier-accepted rational projection identity or one verifier-accepted common signed response-row contrast.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen primitives do not prove that target constancy on fibers of the polynomial observation map implies a rational circuit in the finite projection library; a fiber-constant target can in principle descend only as a nonrational algebraic function. On the negative side, the ordinary hedge perturbation and the terminal tensor contrast need not lift through several interacting districts, fixed kernels, and observed descendants without changing at least one supported observed cell. This is exactly the sibling open question on which the unchanged headline depends.
obligation.attempted: The Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser recursive district and fixing construction was compiled on the projection side, and the Kivva--Mokhtarian--Etesami--Kiyavash positivity strategy was pursued on the witness side. Rational interior mixing closes the ordinary hedge case and the presolve closes the terminal three-observable case. For a general residual, however, the common contrast must lie simultaneously in the kernels of all context observation maps while retaining nonzero target derivative; neither districtwise contrasts nor generic elimination prove that common-kernel alternative or exclude a nonrational identified quotient.
obligation.partial_result:
The normalization equivalence, local transition soundness, denominator positivity, and lexicographic decrease are established.  The initial-token compiler and nonresidual-progress lemma now show that the deterministic machine cannot stop before a residual-ready state, and the published-trace lemma proves preservation of every successful Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser derivation using only \(H\).  Certificate soundness proves
\[
F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta)
\Longrightarrow
T_{a,H}\text{ is constant on every }O_H\text{-fiber},
\]
whereas any returned twin box exhibits a nonconstant fiber.  The ordinary no-selection residual is completely compiled to a Shpitser--Pearl formula or a strictly positive rational hedge-twin box.  What remains is the converse at a general fixed-support residual: proving that fiber constancy forces one of the finite rational projection identities, and that failure of fiber constancy forces one common signed response-row contrast that survives all interacting districts, fixed kernels, and observed descendants while preserving exactly \(H\).
